payload.title: [auth-core-4] forgot-password throttle keyed by victim email enables targeted reset-lockout DoS
payload.description:
AUDIT FINDING auth-core-4 (low/dos, confidence=medium, verify-votes +2/-0)

FILE: apps/server/src/auth/identity-routes.ts
LINES: 1668-1671

WHAT: handleEmailForgotPassword throttles with identifier: email (L1671), and authAttemptKey (server.ts L3038-3041) keys the bucket on route\0tenant\0email when an identity is present. An unauthenticated attacker can deliberately hammer POST /auth/email/forgot-password for a chosen victim address to exhaust that email's bucket, after which the genuine user's legitimate reset request is rejected (or, since the route still returns 200, silently dropped before a token is issued) until the window resets. Because the actor falls back to email rather than IP when an email is supplied, the attacker's own IP does not bound this.

IMPACT: Targeted denial of the password-reset capability for any known/guessed email, for the duration of each rate-limit window, with trivial cost to the attacker.

SUGGESTED FIX: Throttle forgot-password on a composite of email AND client IP (or a separate, more generous per-email issuance counter that does not block on a shared brute-force bucket), so one attacker IP cannot drain a victim's reset allowance.
